newsitem.title: UK: Tesco leads decline in food retail stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tesco leads decline in food retail stocks.

text.p: Shares in Tesco Plc led food retail stocks down on Tuesday on further response to Safeway Plc's recent cautious trading statement and as a retail survey added to gloom in the sector, traders said.
"There is just a lowering of expectations all round," said one dealer.

Traders poured cold water on vague market rumours that one of the leading food retailers could be poised to issue a further gloomy trading statement. "I would take it with a big pinch of salt," said one.

Tesco was down 9p, or 2.6 percent, at 333-1/2 by 1544 GMT in volume of 7.7 million shares, Safeway was down 8p at 349-1/2, ASDA Group Plc was down 2-1/2p at 113-3/4 and J Sainsbury Plc was down 4p at 316-1/2.
Earlier today the British Retail Consortium said food and drink sales were weak in January with the rise in food sales by value marginally lower in the month than in December.
On Monday analysts at BZW cut their earnings estimates for leading food retailers, warning that January had been a difficult month across the industry, sources said.
Last week Safeway rattled the sector with a warning that profits could be hit by a slowdown in sales growth in the first 16 weeks of the second half of its current year.
